newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: Large bookover trade boosts Lenco volumes.
newsitem.headline: Large bookover trade boosts Lenco volumes.

text.p: A hefty number of shares in Lenco Ltd, a South African firm rumoured to be in talks with fellow packaging firm Malbak Ltd, were traded on the Johannesburg Stock Exchange on Friday morning.

Dealers said that 3.1 million shares worth nearly 22 million rand changed hands in a single bookover deal executed by brokerage Deutsche Morgan Grenfell. A bookover occurs where buyer and seller are matched by the same brokerage.
By 1000 GMT Lenco shares were unchanged at overnight closing levels of seven rand. The firm was the biggest volume trader on the bourse on Friday morning.
Speculation has been rife this month that Lenco, which is in the stable of industrial conglomerate Rembrandt Group Ltd (Remgro), may be used as a vehicle by Remgro to takeover over Malbak.
The view is that Remgro will buy stakes in Malbak from financial services giant Sanlam and investment firm Sankorp.

Lenco's executive chairman Douglas de Jager told Reuters earlier in June that the firm was in some unspecified talks which had been notified to shareholders through a cautionary announcement on May 20.
He declined to give further details, saying the talks were at a "very sensitive stage".
Malbak and subsidiary Kohler Ltd have also both issued cautionaries.

Remgro, which already owns a minority stake in Malbak, said earlier this month that it had made no decisions regarding its investment in the company which recently underwent a rigorous unbundling process.
Another theory bandied around is that Malbak could buy Lenco and sell its non-packaging interests.
Lenco last week reported a strong recovery in earnings to 32.93 million rand in the year to end March compared with a loss of 22.12 million rand last year.
